digest.component_or_area: LLM gate cost analysis and ordinal-to-binary review migration
propositions: LLM gate per-run costs since Bedrock switch measure 3.02 dollars plan-review, 1.42 dollars code-review, 2.24 dollars completion-verifier; mean per-ticket completion cost 11.85 dollars

Cheap-model experiments (Nova Pro, Haiku, Nova 2 Lite) rejected Haiku for agentic review and Nova Pro for completion-verifier but identified bounded Nova pilots and terminal-failure fixes as credible cost levers

Code-review ordinal severity axes are structurally inert because blocking is criterion-routed (98.2% disabled) and the 0.95 impact threshold is unreachable (0-occurrence conjunction of system+high+hard across 3,738 gradings); migrating ordinal-to-kind-set is premature without fixing the decision rule first

Deprecation removal-readiness survey found no expiring scheduled removals under current policy; only the gitattributes migration arm is dead; single-pass review surfaces and REBAR_LLM_MODEL are removal-candidates only if a new pre-1.0 breaking window opens

AWS Bedrock Nova client-error spike (77 errors, 94% on Nova family, 2026-08-10/11) traced to MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=10000 validation failures; Claude ladder unaffected and correctly isolated by alarm design

Observability probe defect (widespread-zealous-narwhal, colossal-slothful-grouse) fabricates metric counts from cold-start offset absence and over-broad pattern matching; both false-positive alarm firings on 2026-08-12 are probe-side, not alarm threshold issues
